_note: SYNTHETIC sample data written for this project. The issues are modelled on common, publicly documented Kubernetes failure modes but are not copies of real GitHub issues. Use scripts/fetch_github_issues.py to ingest real public issues instead.

issues.title: Pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff after upgrading containerd to 1.7.20
issues.body: After upgrading containerd from 1.6 to 1.7.20 on our worker nodes, about a third of the pods go into CrashLoopBackOff. kubectl describe shows 'failed to create shim task: OCI runtime create failed'. The kubelet log repeats 'back-off restarting failed container'. Nodes that were not upgraded are fine.
comments: Same here. The node uses cgroup v2 and containerd's config.toml still had SystemdCgroup = false.

Resolution: set SystemdCgroup = true under the runc options in /etc/containerd/config.toml so containerd and the kubelet agree on the systemd cgroup driver, then restart containerd. Pods recover without being recreated.

issues.title: kube-scheduler leaves pods Pending with topologySpreadConstraints on tainted nodes
issues.body: Deployments that use topologySpreadConstraints with whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule stay Pending. The FailedScheduling event says '0/5 nodes are available: 3 node(s) had untolerated taint {dedicated: gpu}, 2 node(s) didn't match pod topology spread constraints'. The tainted GPU nodes are still counted as topology domains.
comments: Workaround: set nodeTaintsPolicy: Honor in the topology spread constraint so tainted nodes the pod cannot tolerate are excluded from the skew calculation.

issues.title: etcd 'mvcc: database space exceeded' makes all API writes fail
issues.body: Every create/update through kube-apiserver returns 'etcdserver: mvcc: database space exceeded'. The etcd alarm list shows NOSPACE. The cluster has many short-lived Jobs and events, and the etcd database reached the default 2 GiB quota.
comments: Resolution: compact to the current revision, run etcdctl defrag on each member, then etcdctl alarm disarm. Long term we raised --quota-backend-bytes to 8 GiB and enabled automatic compaction (--auto-compaction-retention=1h).

issues.title: CoreDNS i/o timeout resolving external names under load
issues.body: During traffic peaks application pods log 'dial udp 10.96.0.10:53: i/o timeout' and CoreDNS logs 'read udp ... i/o timeout' to the upstream resolver. Only 2 CoreDNS replicas run for 120 nodes.
comments: Resolution: scaled CoreDNS with the cluster-proportional-autoscaler, increased the cache plugin TTL to 30s and deployed NodeLocal DNSCache so most lookups never leave the node. Timeouts stopped.

issues.title: kube-state-metrics OOMKilled on large clusters
issues.body: kube-state-metrics restarts every few minutes with reason OOMKilled (exit code 137). The default memory limit of 250Mi is too low for a cluster with 40k pods.
comments: Resolution: raised the memory limit to 1Gi and enabled horizontal sharding (--shard / --total-shards) across 3 replicas.

issues.title: kubelet reports 'PLEG is not healthy' on nodes with many containers
issues.body: Nodes flap between Ready and NotReady. The kubelet log shows 'PLEG is not healthy: pleg was last seen active 3m0s ago; threshold is 3m0s'. These nodes run 200+ containers and use slow network-attached disks; container runtime calls take several seconds.
comments: PLEG (pod lifecycle event generator) relists all containers from the runtime. Slow runtime or disk I/O makes the relist exceed the threshold. Reducing maxPods to 110 and moving /var/lib/containerd to local SSD fixed it for us.

issues.title: ImagePullBackOff from private registry after token rotation
issues.body: After rotating the registry robot token, new pods fail with ErrImagePull then ImagePullBackOff: 'unauthorized: authentication required'. Existing pods keep running because the image is cached.
comments: Resolution: the imagePullSecret in each namespace still had the old token. Recreated the docker-registry secret with the new token; use an external secrets operator to keep it in sync.

issues.title: kube-proxy in IPVS mode drops connections after endpoint updates
issues.body: With kube-proxy in IPVS mode, clients see connection resets for ~1s whenever a backend pod is replaced. Stale conntrack entries keep pointing at the deleted endpoint.
comments: Setting net.ipv4.vs.conntrack=1 and net.ipv4.vs.expire_nodest_conn=1 reduces resets; graceful termination of endpoints is the proper fix.

issues.title: kube-apiserver requests fail with 'context deadline exceeded' when etcd is slow
issues.body: kubectl commands intermittently fail with 'Error from server: etcdserver: request timed out' and apiserver logs 'context deadline exceeded' for etcd calls. etcd metrics show wal_fsync_duration p99 above 500ms.
comments: Resolution: etcd shared a disk with container logs. Moving the etcd data dir to a dedicated SSD brought fsync p99 under 10ms and the deadline errors disappeared.

issues.title: HPA not scaling: unable to get metrics for resource cpu
issues.body: HorizontalPodAutoscaler shows <unknown>/50% and events say 'failed to get cpu utilization: unable to get metrics for resource cpu'. metrics-server logs 'x509: cannot validate certificate because it doesn't contain any IP SANs' when scraping kubelets.
comments: Resolution: enabled kubelet serving certificate rotation so kubelet certs include the node IP, and approved the pending CSRs. --kubelet-insecure-tls also works but is not recommended.

issues.title: Nodes go NotReady after kubelet client certificate expires
issues.body: Exactly one year after cluster creation, several nodes became NotReady. The kubelet log shows 'x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid' when talking to the API server.
comments: Resolution: set rotateCertificates: true in the KubeletConfiguration so the kubelet requests a new client certificate before expiry; for already expired nodes, re-bootstrap the kubelet with a new bootstrap token.

issues.title: ingress-nginx returns 502 Bad Gateway during rolling updates
issues.body: During every Deployment rollout ingress-nginx returns a burst of 502 Bad Gateway. The controller still routes to pods that already received SIGTERM.
comments: Resolution: add a preStop hook (sleep 10) and a readinessProbe so the pod is removed from endpoints before the app stops accepting connections.

issues.title: PVC stays Pending: waiting for first consumer to be created before binding
issues.body: A new PersistentVolumeClaim stays Pending with the event 'waiting for first consumer to be created before binding'.
comments: This is expected: the StorageClass uses volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer, so the volume is provisioned only when a pod using the claim is scheduled. Create the pod and the PVC binds.

issues.title: kubelet evicts pods with DiskPressure on log-heavy nodes
issues.body: Pods are evicted with 'The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage' and the node gets the DiskPressure condition. A chatty sidecar writes several GB of stdout logs per hour.
comments: Set containerLogMaxSize: 50Mi and containerLogMaxFiles: 3 in the kubelet config, and add ephemeral-storage limits to the noisy containers.

issues.title: CoreDNS CrashLoopBackOff: Loop detected for zone
issues.body: CoreDNS pods are in CrashLoopBackOff. Logs show '[FATAL] plugin/loop: Loop (127.0.0.1:43851 -> :53) detected for zone "."'. The nodes run systemd-resolved, so /etc/resolv.conf points to 127.0.0.53.
comments: Resolution: point the kubelet --resolv-conf at /run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf (the real upstream servers) instead of the stub resolver, then restart CoreDNS.

issues.title: Scheduler throughput drops on 5000-node clusters
issues.body: kube-scheduler schedules only ~30 pods/s on a 5000-node cluster and the FailedScheduling backlog grows during batch jobs.
comments: Lower percentageOfNodesToScore (for example to 10) so the scheduler stops scoring after enough feasible nodes are found, and raise the client QPS/burst.

issues.title: Frequent etcd leader elections across availability zones
issues.body: etcd logs 'etcdserver: leader changed' several times per hour and apiserver requests briefly fail. Control-plane nodes are spread across zones with 15-30ms RTT.
comments: Tune --heartbeat-interval to about the RTT (e.g. 100ms) and --election-timeout to 10x that (1000ms). Check that disk fsync latency is also low.

issues.title: Job podFailurePolicy ignored when backoffLimit is reached
issues.body: A Job with podFailurePolicy action Ignore for exit code 42 still fails once backoffLimit is reached. kube-controller-manager counts the ignored failures toward the backoff limit.
comments: Confirmed on 1.31. Pods must have restartPolicy: Never for podFailurePolicy to apply; with OnFailure the policy is skipped.

issues.title: kube-apiserver OOMKilled during large LIST requests
issues.body: A monitoring tool lists all pods in all namespaces without pagination every 10s. kube-apiserver memory spikes and the process is OOMKilled.
comments: Resolution: make clients use pagination (limit/continue) and watch instead of polling LIST, and configure API Priority and Fairness to cap the tool's concurrency.

issues.title: kubectl logs fails: tls: failed to verify certificate
issues.body: kubectl logs and kubectl exec return 'Error from server: Get https://10.0.1.5:10250/...: tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority'.
comments: Resolution: enable serverTLSBootstrap in the kubelet config and approve the kubelet-serving CSRs so the kubelet serves a cert signed by the cluster CA.

issues.title: Slow DNS lookups because of ndots:5
issues.body: Each external lookup (api.example.com) produces 5 failed search-domain queries before the real one, adding latency and load on CoreDNS.
comments: Resolution: set dnsConfig.options ndots: 2 on the pod spec, or use fully qualified names with a trailing dot.

issues.title: Containers OOMKilled although working set is below the memory limit (cgroup v2)
issues.body: Java pods are OOMKilled with exit code 137 while container_memory_working_set_bytes is 70% of the limit. Nodes moved to cgroup v2. Page cache from heavy file I/O seems to count toward the limit.
comments: Size the JVM heap with -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=70 and leave headroom for page cache and off-heap memory; newer kernels reclaim page cache before OOM more reliably.

issues.title: kube-proxy high CPU in iptables mode with 10k Services
issues.body: kube-proxy in iptables mode uses a full core and syncs take 20s+ on a cluster with 10,000 Services, delaying endpoint updates.
comments: Switch kube-proxy to IPVS or nftables mode, which scale much better with many Services, and raise --iptables-min-sync-period if you must stay on iptables.

issues.title: Pods not terminated gracefully when a node shuts down
issues.body: When a node is shut down for maintenance, pods are killed immediately and stateful apps lose in-flight work.
comments: Resolution: enable graceful node shutdown by setting shutdownGracePeriod: 60s and shutdownGracePeriodCriticalPods: 20s in the KubeletConfiguration; the kubelet then delays shutdown via systemd inhibitor locks.
